# 2 Chronicles Chapter 29 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Hezekiah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.

**2** He did what was right in the LORD's eyes, just as his ancestor David had done.

**3** In the first month of the first year of his reign, he reopened the doors of the LORD's temple and repaired them.

**4** He brought in the priests and Levites and assembled them in the square on the east side.

**5** He said, "Listen to me, Levites! Consecrate yourselves now, and consecrate the temple of the LORD, the God of your ancestors. Remove everything defiled from the sanctuary.

**6** Our ancestors were unfaithful and did what was evil in the LORD our God's sight. They abandoned Him, turned their faces away from His dwelling place, and turned their backs on Him.

**7** They even shut the doors of the portico, put out the lamps, and stopped burning incense and presenting burnt offerings in the sanctuary to the God of Israel.

**8** That is why the LORD's wrath fell on Judah and Jerusalem. He made them an object of dread, horror, and scorn, as you can see with your own eyes.

**9** This is why our ancestors have fallen by the sword, and our sons, daughters, and wives have been taken captive.

**10** Now I intend to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that His fierce anger will turn away from us.

**11** My sons, don't be negligent now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before Him, to serve Him, and to be His ministers and burn incense."

**12** Then the Levites got to work: from the Kohathites — Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah; from the Merarites — Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; from the Gershonites — Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;

**13** from the descendants of Elizaphan — Shimri and Jeiel; from the descendants of Asaph — Zechariah and Mattaniah;

**14** from the descendants of Heman — Jehiel and Shimei; from the descendants of Jeduthun — Shemaiah and Uzziel.

**15** They gathered their fellow Levites and consecrated themselves. Then, following the king's orders based on the LORD's word, they went in to purify the LORD's temple.

**16** The priests entered the inner part of the LORD's temple to purify it. They brought out to the temple courtyard everything unclean they found inside. The Levites then took it and carried it out to the Kidron Valley.

**17** They began the consecration on the first day of the first month. By the eighth day they had reached the portico of the LORD. For eight more days they consecrated the LORD's temple itself. They finished on the sixteenth day of the first month.

**18** Then they went to King Hezekiah and reported: "We have purified the entire temple of the LORD — the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the table of the Presence with all its utensils.

**19** We have recovered and consecrated all the articles that King Ahaz threw out during his unfaithful reign. They are now in front of the LORD's altar."

**20** Early the next morning King Hezekiah gathered the city officials and went up to the LORD's temple.

**21** They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. He ordered the Aaronic priests to offer them on the LORD's altar.

**22** They slaughtered the bulls, and the priests splashed the blood on the altar. Then they slaughtered the rams and splashed their blood on the altar. Then they slaughtered the lambs and splashed their blood on the altar.

**23** The goats for the sin offering were brought before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.

**24** The priests slaughtered the goats and put their blood on the altar as a sin offering to atone for all Israel, because the king had ordered the burnt offering and sin offering to be made for all Israel.

**25** He stationed the Levites in the LORD's temple with cymbals, harps, and lyres, following the instructions of David, Gad the king's seer, and Nathan the prophet — for these instructions had come from the LORD through His prophets.

**26** The Levites stood ready with David's instruments, and the priests with their trumpets.

**27** Hezekiah gave the order to sacrifice the burnt offering on the altar. As the offering began, singing to the LORD also began, accompanied by the trumpets and the instruments of David king of Israel.

**28** The whole assembly worshiped, the singers sang, and the trumpeters played. All this continued until the burnt offering was finished.

**29** When the offerings were complete, the king and everyone present with him knelt down and worshiped.

**30** King Hezekiah and the officials told the Levites to praise the LORD with the words of David and of Asaph the seer. They sang praises with gladness and bowed down and worshiped.

**31** Then Hezekiah said, "You have now dedicated yourselves to the LORD. Come and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the LORD's temple." So the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and all whose hearts were willing brought burnt offerings.

**32** The assembly brought 70 bulls, 100 rams, and 200 lambs as burnt offerings to the LORD.

**33** The animals consecrated as sacrifices totaled 600 bulls and 3,000 sheep and goats.

**34** There weren't enough priests to skin all the burnt offerings, so their relatives the Levites helped them until the work was done and more priests had consecrated themselves — for the Levites had been more conscientious about consecrating themselves than the priests had.

**35** There were also abundant burnt offerings, along with the fat of the fellowship offerings and the drink offerings for the burnt offerings. So the service of the LORD's temple was reestablished.

**36** Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced at what God had done for the people, because it had all happened so quickly.


---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **29:3**: First day of the first month of his first year — Hezekiah doesn't wait. His father locked the temple; Hezekiah's first act is to unlock it. The symbolism could not be clearer.

- **29:11**: "Don't be negligent" — Hezekiah lights a fire under the Levites. He knows that national revival requires institutional momentum, and institutions only move when someone pushes them.

- **29:24**: "For all Israel" — not just Judah. Hezekiah makes atonement for the entire nation, including the north, which has already fallen to Assyria. This is either naive or visionary. The Chronicler thinks it's visionary.

- **29:36**: "It had all happened so quickly" — the speed catches everyone off guard. Sixteen days from locked doors to full-scale worship. Sometimes renewal doesn't take decades. Sometimes it takes one leader who refuses to wait.


— PNEUMA
